audit_findings.title: Valuation date is post-Ultra close, but the earnings and balance-sheet inputs are pre-close
audit_findings.magnitude: $720 million filed purchase price; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the equity bridge through cash, borrowing, assumed liabilities and transaction costs, and changes future OE through acquired earnings and incremental interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Unless otherwise indicated, information contained in this Annual Report is as of March 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-date error: the September 5 valuation treats the transaction as pending even though the supplied record says it closed August 24. Because neither the post-close financing nor the acquired business is represented, the direction is mixed, but the omitted transaction is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing statement and first post-close balance sheet, then rerun the bridge, share count and OE forecast using actual consideration, financing, assumed liabilities, transaction costs and acquired operating results.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 owner earnings likely capitalize a nonrecurring tax windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 tax expense was $11 million versus $198.3 million at the prior-year 23% rate, a computed $187.3 million gap; disclosed favorable components include $80 million from uncertain-tax-position changes, $103 million of R&D and other credits, and $29 million of FDII benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nonrecurring tax benefit retained in the $796.4 million OE anchor is compounded through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in tax expense was primarily driven by a reduction in the income tax reserve related to the completion of the IRS examination procedures and the tax benefit recognized in the third quarter as a result of a higher-than-estimated research and development tax credit and additional foreign derived intangible income deductions.
audit_findings.explanation: The unusually low tax expense is demonstrated, but its inclusion in anchor OE is unresolved because no OE-to-net-income reconciliation was supplied. Materiality is clear: even an unnormalized recurring overstatement of $80 million would, at the base operating-value-to-anchor multiple, represent about $1.33 billion or $10.41 per share before the margin of safety and could reverse the buy-below conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $796.4 million anchor to reported net income line by line, separate recurring credits from reserve releases and refund-related items, and rerun all scenarios with only recurring tax benefits.

audit_findings.title: The bridge omits the $248 million claimed-cost liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $248 million, equal to $1.95 per diluted share and 1.75% of base equity value; a full bridge deduction would reduce the computed buy-below price from $78.02 to about $76.66, still $3.86 above the $72.80 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: A settlement cash outflow not captured in forecast OE would require a debt-like deduction from the equity bridge; deducting it when provisions already reduced OE would double count it.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company had recorded liabilities (included in accounts payable and other accrued expenses) of approximately $ 248 million and $ 245 million, respectively, for estimated adjustments to claimed costs based on its historical DCAA audit results, including the final resolution of such audits with the Defense Contract Management Agency (“DCMA”), for claimed costs incurred subsequent to fiscal 2011.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its omission from the stated bridge are demonstrated, but whether a deduction is appropriate is unresolved. Even the conservative full deduction does not independently change the stated valuation conclusion, providing a concrete basis for treating it as not material in isolation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the reserve's historical income-statement charges, expected refunds or billing offsets, and forecast cash treatment; rerun only the portion not already reflected in normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: Existing underfunded postretirement obligations may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $180 million filed obligation, equal to $1.41 per diluted share and 1.27% of base equity value; a full deduction would reduce the computed buy-below price to about $77.03, still $4.23 above market
audit_findings.mechanism: Benefit payments not already represented by service cost, interest cost or forecast cash expenses would reduce the equity bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognizes a liability on the consolidated balance sheets within other long-term liabilities for the defined benefit plans' underfunded status, measures the defined benefit plans' obligations that determine its funded status as of the end of the fiscal year, and recognizes the gains and losses and prior service costs and credits as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income for the changes in the defined benefit plans' funded status that are not recognized as components of net periodic benefit cost.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated, but the omitted economic amount is less than $180 million if forecast OE already includes relevant benefit costs. Even deducting the entire obligation would not independently change the buy-below conclusion. Filed expected payments are $110 million through fiscal 2036, further limiting the immediate economic scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile plan liabilities, service and interest costs, and expected benefit payments against forecast OE; deduct only settlements not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Investment stakes may have been added without netting contractual capital calls
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed commitments were $247 million at June 30, down from $322 million at March 31; $247 million equals $1.94 per diluted share and 1.74% of base equity value, and a full deduction would reduce buy-below to about $76.66, still $3.86 above market
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds the $452 million investment carrying value, while any negative net value of remaining capital calls should reduce stakes_net or future cash available to shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026, the Company’s unfunded capital commitments as a limited partner in the Funds was $ 322 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The outstanding calls are demonstrated, but face commitments are not automatically liabilities of equal economic loss because contributions purchase additional fund interests. Even the conservative treatment of deducting the entire latest commitment without credit for acquired assets would not independently reverse the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain fund-level carrying values, remaining commitments, call schedules and current valuations, then calculate stakes_net as the present value of distributions and residual interests less future calls.

audit_findings.title: The positive growth cases require a sharp reversal of current operating deterioration
audit_findings.magnitude: Base value exceeds bear by $29.27 per share, and bull exceeds bear by $41.28 per share; applying the same 30% margin of safety to the $82.19 bear value gives about $57.53, below the $72.80 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: The 6% and 8% growth assumptions increase annual OE and terminal value, which represents 51.5% and 52.6% of operating value in those cases.
audit_findings.evidence: Revenue decreased 6% to $11,217 million, primarily driven by the impact of a slowed procurement and funding environment, including the government shutdown that occurred in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Growth is a forecast uncertainty rather than a demonstrated calculation error, but it is presently material to the decision. Revenue fell 6% in FY2026 and another 4% in the June quarter, although June-quarter operating income increased 9% and backlog increased 3%. The record therefore does not establish that recovery is impossible, but reliance on positive growth determines whether the margin-of-safety purchase test is met.
audit_findings.action: Build and rerun contract-level organic growth cases using funded backlog conversion, recompetes, pricing, headcount and margins; separately model Ultra contributions, purchase financing and integration costs.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2023 residual D&A was $42.7 million, 25.8% of filed D&A and 6.7% of FY2023 OE; effect on the FY2026 anchor is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be a non-economic charge would be added back to OE and would increase forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $42.7m (25.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement is indicated because the uncertain amount was left as an expense. The FY2023 amount shows a potentially meaningful conservative bias, but the record does not identify the residual components or establish a recurring FY2026 amount, so current materiality cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the D&A schedule by asset class for each valuation year, classify only demonstrably non-economic amortization or depreciation as eligible, and rerun the valuation if a recurring eligible amount is established.
